A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PuDDing research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–C. Retained and added material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, inference timings, pruning-pattern analyses, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark comparisons, edge-device timings, multidomain calibration experiments, and quantization tests.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the same candidate-set generation, task-likelihood losses, BERT-based MSE router, and per-prompt selection procedure. The new multidomain and AWQ experiments vary calibration data and numerical precision without documenting changes to PuDDing's pruning or routing rules.

E1.justification: Table 5 adds PubMedQA and SciQ evaluation. Appendix B.4 also broadens calibration beyond commonsense reasoning: its new variant uses MathQA, PubMedQA, and SciQ alongside ARC-Easy and WinoGrande. This substantially expands the training and evaluation coverage across mathematics, biomedical, and science tasks.

E2.justification: V3 Table 4 adds LLM-Streamline (with fine-tuning) to the seven-block pruning comparison alongside SLEB, Shortened LLaMA, and PuDDing. The existing baseline comparisons are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: V3 adds Apple M3 Pro timing settings and W8A16/W4A16 AWQ experiments. Appendix B.4 introduces a matched-sample-size control when changing calibration composition. Existing training settings remain unchanged. V3 removes the explicit five-subtask MMLU description without specifying a replacement, leaving that evaluation protocol unclear.

E4.justification: New Appendices B.4–B.5 substantially extend the analyses to two additional questions: sensitivity to calibration-domain composition and compatibility with 8-bit/4-bit quantization. The original omission-set-count, task-likelihood, and router-loss ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, reports confidence intervals or error bars, or supplies significance tests. The added results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3 adds benchmark, baseline, edge-timing, multidomain, and quantization results. LLM-Streamline averages 66.08% in Table 4; Table 13 reports 61.28% versus 62.37% for original versus multidomain PuDDing; Table 14 reports 61.68% and 58.58% with 8-bit and 4-bit AWQ. Table 2 corrects the margin from +2.95 to +4.69 points while retaining 61.93% accuracy. MMLU values change, including PuDDing's 33.63% to 39.00%, but the missing subset specification prevents treating this as a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, constraints, and loss definitions in Equations 1–13 are retained. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about task-dependent block importance, novel prompt-based depth pruning, improved accuracy over static pruning, and computational efficiency. New experiments support these existing claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: Section 3 corrects the block-knowledge interpretation: block 29, rather than 30, is associated with BoolQ. V3 adds interpretations concerning edge-device suitability, domain-specific calibration, and quantization compatibility. Existing limitations remain unchanged. Appendix B.5's claim of no 8-bit degradation is stronger than its reported 61.93% versus 61.68% averages support.

D1.justification: V3 adds project/code access links, identifies M3 Pro hardware and AWQ precisions, and documents the multidomain calibration composition and sample-size control. Original implementation details remain. Conversely, the named five-subtask MMLU specification is removed without replacement details.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 replaces the width-pruning side note with explicit contextual-sparsity positioning, adding ShadowLLM, Sirius, and CATS alongside the previously cited Deja Vu. Appendix B.5 adds AWQ. FLAP and SliceGPT remain cited elsewhere; other bibliography changes largely update formatting or publication metadata.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites and retitles Section 2.3, adds two appendix subsections and acknowledgements, and updates publication information and bibliography presentation. Most existing scientific prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 7, 13, and 14, expands Tables 4–5, and relocates the parameter-transfer table as Table 8. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and Figure 5 moves lower on its page. All figure artwork and the general layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The M3 Pro measurements strengthen the on-device motivation, while broader domain coverage and calibration/quantization analyses improve practical evidence. Code pointers, the corrected accuracy margin, and the corrected block interpretation also help. These gains are tempered by the unspecified revised MMLU scope, limited documentation of new comparisons, and the overstated claim of no 8-bit degradation.
